url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

**Triangulation Metrics – A Quick Overview** | What | Why it matters | Typical use‑cases | |------|----------------|-------------------| | **Definition** | Triangulation metrics quantify the accuracy, precision, and reliability of distance measurements obtained through triangulation—determining a point’s location by measuring angles from known reference points. | • Surveying and mapping
• Geodetic network maintenance
• Remote sensing calibration | | **Key Parameters** | • **Baseline length** – distance between two known stations.
• **Angle measurement error** – instrument precision.
• **Atmospheric refraction correction** – affects angle readings.
• **Baseline orientation** – influences error propagation. | • Baseline selection strategy
• Error budgeting for high‑precision projects | | **Common Metrics** | • **Standard Deviation (σ)** – spread of repeated measurements.
• **Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)** – overall fit quality.
• **Dilution of Precision (DOP)** – geometric strength of the network.
• **Residual Analysis** – checks for systematic biases. | • Network adjustment diagnostics
• Quality control reports | | **Why It Matters** | Accurate triangulation metrics ensure that derived coordinates meet required tolerances, reduce uncertainty in downstream analyses, and help identify problematic stations or instruments early. | • Legal land boundary determinations
• Infrastructure alignment
• Scientific research requiring sub‑centimeter accuracy | In short, triangulation metrics provide the statistical and geometric tools needed to assess and improve the quality of triangulated coordinate networks.
